text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Moslem-Croat federation House of People failed to approve draft law modifying boundaries of municipalities which was already adopted by the federation House of Representatives. Deputies agreed to form a working group to resolve the dispute by May 24.
- Talks between Moslem Party of Democratic Action and Croat Democratic Union fail to produce an agreement on structure of municipality for divided town of Mostar, newspaper says.
- Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe releases preliminary figures for voter registration for municipal elections in September. OSCE says 122,460 people have registered so far.
- The Islamic community in Bosnia has joined humanitarian efforts for Iran after earthquake which shook the country last week, Moslem religious leader Mustafa Efendija Ceric said.
- Deputy Minister of Defence Sakib Mahmuljin denies reports that Bosnian army Fourth Corps will be integrated into Croat militia in the region of Mostar.

- The Moslem Party for Democratic Action threatens to boycott upcoming local polls in September if the OSCE and international supervisor for Brcko refuse to change rules for voter registration in town of Brcko, SDA party official says.

- United Nations envoy to Bosnia, Kai Eide, expresses concern over slow pace of the implementation of the Dayton peace agreement and says responsibility lies with political leaders who have not changed their fundamental political attitude.
- International Police Task Force (IPTF) says it has launched policy which requires local police to remove illegal check-points which limit freedom of movement in Bosnia.
- After nine months, Bosnian expert team for missing people resumes exhumation of victims from Srebrenica killed in Serb offensive of July 1995, newspaper reports.
- Federation High Court decides to try opposition member Ibrahim Djedovic in Sarajevo instead of Bihac as an alleged war crimes suspect. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +377-71-663-864
